story_title: Lina and Adams and the Head to Toes Game
title: Lina and Adams and the Head to Toes Game 👋 | Body Parts in English for Kids | Moon Tales Kids
description:
Play a fun game with Lina, Adams and Milo, and help find Adams's lost hat! 👋👀👂
In this English story for kids, children learn 7 new words — body parts: head, eyes, ears, nose, mouth, hands and feet. Listen, repeat, and learn English with Lina, Adams and Milo the cat.

📚 New words in this story:
🧢 head — الرأس — la tête
👀 eyes — العينان — les yeux
👂 ears — الأذنان — les oreilles
👃 nose — الأنف — le nez
👄 mouth — الفم — la bouche
👐 hands — اليدان — les mains
🦶 feet — القدمان — les pieds

👨‍👩‍👧 For parents: play "touch your nose, touch your head" with your child after the story. Pause after each new word and say it out loud. Perfect for ages 3 to 8 and for children learning English as a second language.

🇲🇦 قصة باللغة الإنجليزية للأطفال لتعلم أعضاء الجسم بطريقة ممتعة.

lines.text: It is a bright morning at school.
Lina and Adams sit in the classroom. Milo the cat peeks in. Meow!
Look at the board! It says: Head to Toes!
What does it mean?
Today, the children will play a fun game about the body.
When I say a body word, you touch it. Ready?
Ready!
Ready! This will be fun!
The first word is: head!
Lina and Adams put their hands on top of their heads.
My hat goes on my head. Look!
My hair is on my head too!
Your head is at the top of your body.
Say it with me: head!
Milo touches his head with his paw. Meow!
The next word is: eyes!
I see with my eyes. I can see a book!
I can see Milo! He is blinking at me.
We have two eyes. We use our eyes to see.
Open your eyes. Close your eyes. Open them again!
Can you say it? Eyes!
Tweet, tweet! What is that sound?
I hear a bird! It is singing at the window.
I hear it with my ears!
We have two ears. We use our ears to hear.
Touch your ears. Can you hear the little bird?
Say it with me: ears!
Milo moves his pointy ears. He hears the bird too.
Now the word is: nose!
Mmm! I smell a flower with my nose.
It smells sweet. Like honey!
Your nose is in the middle of your face. We smell with our nose.
Touch your nose. Boop!
Let's say it together: nose!
Milo sniffs the flower. Achoo! Everybody laughs.
At lunch time, Lina and Adams go home to eat.
I am hungry! I open my mouth. Big bite!
I eat my apple with my mouth. Crunch, crunch!
We eat, we talk, and we smile with our mouth.
Can you open your mouth wide? Now close it.
Say it with me: mouth!
Milo licks his little mouth. Yum!
After lunch, the friends go to the park.
Catch the ball, Adams! Use your hands!
I caught it! Now I will throw it back.
We have two hands. We catch, we clap and we wave with our hands.
Clap your hands with Lina and Adams. Clap, clap, clap!
Can you say it? Hands!
Now it is time to run.
I put on my shoes. Shoes go on my feet!
Let's run with our feet. One, two, three, go!
Lina and Adams run on the grass. Milo runs too, on four little paws.
We stand, walk, run and jump with our feet.
Stamp your feet! Stamp, stamp! Say it: feet!
Whoosh! A big wind blows in the park.
Oh no! My hat! It flew off my head!
The hat flies up, up, and far away.
I can't see it. Where is my hat?
Don't be sad, Adams. We will find it together.
Let's use our eyes, our ears and our hands!
Okay! Let's look!
Lina uses her eyes. She looks high and low.
Adams uses his ears. Tweet, tweet! The bird is singing near the bench.
Listen! The bird is over there.
Milo sniffs with his nose. Sniff, sniff. Meow!
Look! Milo found it! The hat is next to the bench!
Adams picks up the hat with his hands and puts it on his head.
Thank you, Lina! Thank you, Milo! We are a great team!
Now Adams has his hat again. Let's play the game one more time!
Touch your head! Touch your eyes!
Touch your ears! Touch your nose!
Open your mouth! Clap your hands!
Stamp your feet! Stamp, stamp!
Well done! You know so many body words!
Milo rolls on the grass. He is happy too. Meow!
At night, Lina and Adams are ready for bed.
Today my hat flew away, but we found it together.
We used our eyes, our ears, our nose and our hands!
Milo curls up at their feet. Purr, purr.
Close your eyes now. It is time to sleep.
Good night, Milo.
Good night, everyone!
